title: Patching Array
description: Brute force to optimized: recomputing all subset sums after each patch versus tracking a single "miss" boundary and greedily patching with exactly that value.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given a sorted integer array nums and an integer n, add/patch elements to nums so that any number in the range [1, n] can be formed as the sum of some subset of the (possibly patched) array. Return the MINIMUM number of patches required.

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Every value up to some range must be a subset sum, minimize additions\"","Track \"miss,\" the smallest value NOT yet reachable; if the next number is too large, patch with exactly \"miss\" itself"],["A greedy, provably optimal patching strategy","Always patch with the LARGEST possible value that keeps the reachable range contiguous, which is exactly \"miss\""]]}

blocks.text: If every value from 1 up to some value "miss - 1" is currently achievable as a subset sum, then adding a new number x (or letting an existing array number contribute) extends the achievable range: if x is at most "miss," the achievable range extends contiguously to "miss + x - 1"; if x is greater than "miss," a gap exists at "miss" itself, requiring a patch there.

blocks.title: Analogy: Filling In Missing Denominations to Make Any Amount of Change
blocks.text: Picture having a set of coin denominations and wanting to guarantee you can make exact change for ANY amount up to some target, adding the fewest extra denominations possible. If your current coins let you make every amount up to some value, and the next coin you have is too large to bridge that gap, you must invent a new coin of EXACTLY that missing value to continue the unbroken coverage.

blocks.caption: Track "miss," the smallest unreachable sum; patch with exactly "miss" whenever the next number is too large

blocks.text: Result: 1. With [1,3], achievable sums are 1,3,4. Patching with 2 gives 1,2,3,4,5,6, covering [1,6] with just 1 patch.

Before trying different patch values and rechecking full coverage each time, notice that tracking a single value, "miss" (the smallest sum not yet achievable), lets the greedy strategy be determined directly: if the next available number is small enough to extend coverage, use it for free; otherwise, patch with exactly "miss" itself, which optimally doubles the achievable range.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: If every value from 1 to miss-1 is currently achievable, and the next number available (either from nums or a patch) is at most miss, then every value up to (miss + that number - 1) becomes achievable, since the new number can be combined with any existing achievable sum.

Observation 2: If the next available number from nums exceeds miss, there is no way to reach miss itself using existing numbers, so a patch must be added; the BEST possible patch value is exactly miss itself (using anything smaller would waste potential coverage, and anything larger would leave miss still unreachable).

Observation 3: Patching with exactly miss doubles the achievable range (extending coverage to 2*miss - 1), which is the best possible single patch.

Observation 4: Repeating this process, either consuming the next array number (if small enough) or adding a patch (doubling miss), continues until miss exceeds n, at which point the count of patches used is the minimum needed.

This leads to a single pass: track miss (starting at 1); if the next array number is at most miss, consume it and extend miss; otherwise, patch with miss itself (doubling it) and increment the patch count. Continue until miss exceeds n.
Try patching with various values one at a time, recomputing the full set of achievable subset sums after each patch, until every value in [1,n] is covered.

items: Compute the current set of achievable subset sums from nums (and any patches added so far).
Find the smallest value in [1,n] not yet achievable.
Add a patch (trying, for instance, that missing value) and recompute achievable sums; repeat until everything in [1,n] is covered.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Recomputing achievable subset sums directly and repeatedly checking for gaps correctly identifies where patches are needed.
Computing all subset sums costs exponential time in the number of elements, repeated after every patch, making this extremely slow.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: exponential (recomputing all subset sums repeatedly).
Space: exponential, for storing all achievable sums.

Limitation: tracking only the single value "miss" (rather than the full set of achievable sums) captures everything needed for the greedy decision, achieving O(n + log(max value)) instead of exponential recomputation.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why tracking the full achievable set is unnecessary: only the BOUNDARY of contiguous coverage (the smallest unreachable value, "miss") ever matters for deciding the next action, not the full set of individually achievable sums.

The greedy patch choice: whenever a patch is needed (the next array number exceeds miss), the OPTIMAL patch value is exactly miss itself, since it exactly extends coverage to 2*miss-1 without wasting any potential range.

Consuming array numbers for free: whenever the next array number is small enough (at most miss), it can be used to extend coverage without needing a patch at all.

The core idea: track just "miss," greedily consuming array numbers when possible, patching with exactly "miss" (doubling it) otherwise, until miss exceeds n.

Track miss=1, a pointer into nums, and a patch counter. While miss <= n: if the next nums value is <= miss, consume it (extend miss by that value); otherwise, patch with miss itself (double miss, increment patch count).

blocks.caption: Track only "miss," consuming array numbers or patching with exactly "miss" as needed

blocks.text: The invariant "every value from 1 to miss-1 is achievable" is maintained throughout: consuming an array number <= miss extends this contiguous coverage to miss + that number - 1 (since it can be added to any already-achievable sum), and patching with exactly miss (the smallest currently unreachable value) is provably the best possible single patch, extending coverage to exactly 2*miss - 1, the maximum possible extension without leaving any gap. Repeating this until miss exceeds n guarantees every value in [1,n] becomes achievable, using the minimum number of patches.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(m + log(n)), m being nums.length, since miss at least doubles with each patch.
Space: O(1) extra.

blocks.text: Patching Array is an elegant example of tracking just the BOUNDARY of achievable coverage ("miss"), rather than the full set of achievable values, letting an O(m + log n) greedy algorithm replace an exponential brute force entirely.

items: Patching with a value other than exactly "miss" (e.g., something smaller), which would waste potential coverage extension.
Forgetting to still consume array numbers whenever they qualify (<=miss), unnecessarily adding extra patches instead of using free array elements.

blocks.text: Explicitly proving why patching with exactly "miss" is optimal (any smaller value cannot reach miss itself; any larger value leaves a gap at miss) is the rigorous greedy argument that should be stated clearly before coding.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "cover every value up to n with minimum additions to a set", think: track the smallest currently unreachable value, and patch with exactly that value when needed.

items: How would you also report WHICH values were used as patches, not just the count?
How would this change if patches had varying costs instead of all counting equally?

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: Recomputing all subset sums after each patch costs exponential time; tracking "miss" and greedily consuming/patching costs O(m + log n) time and O(1) space, the standard efficient solution.

items: Pattern: track only the boundary of achievable coverage ("miss"), greedily extending it via free array numbers or optimal patches.
Core Idea: if the next array number is at most miss, consume it for free; otherwise, patch with exactly miss (doubling it) and count the patch.
Time: exponential for recomputing all subset sums, O(m + log n) for the optimized greedy approach.
Most Important Observation: patching with exactly "miss" is provably the optimal single patch, extending coverage the furthest possible without any gap.
Interview Difficulty: a clever, non-obvious greedy problem rewarding recognition of the "miss" invariant.
One line memory trick: track "miss"; consume array numbers that fit, else patch with exactly "miss".
